_comment: How body parts, like alternative limbs, are generated for each group of body plan slots they may fill. A brief's "slots" pick the group by their names without the side (".L"); only the left side is generated, and the right is its mirror. Its images are painted over a front render of the male mannequin at rest, in its A pose, only inside a mask of the brief's slots grown "maskGrow" pixels outward (a mechanical limb may be bulkier than the arm), never into the rest of the body and never past the line of each outer seam, so the neighboring body stays the mannequin's and the part can join its ring; steered by the render's depth. "prompt" fills in {description} and keeps the rest of the body bare and gray; "guideStrength" and "guideEnd" are how hard the depth steers and for what share of the steps (less lets a part's shape stray further from the arm's); "isolated" paints the part over a render of its slots alone instead, as an object on its own named by "piece", which TRELLIS meshes with all its detail rather than as a slice of the whole figure, its turn worked out by fit_body.py (a brief's "fit" may set it false to paint over the whole limb, as "prompt" asks); "roll" turns an isolated part's render that many degrees counterclockwise, slanting a leg like an arm in the A pose (TRELLIS takes a leg standing straight up on its own for one of a pair, and makes both, or hips); "triangles" is the budget for the fitted mesh, and "voxel" the size, in meters, it is rebuilt at before being reduced to it (finer than clothing's 5 mm for arms and hands, so gaps between bones, plates and fingers survive; whole legs keep 5 mm, as finer rebuilds of a leg's armor panels reduce to slivers folded over each other). A brief's "fit" replaces any of these. Skin-like areas will tint with the character's skin channel; "palette" is the channel the part's main other tint group takes, like metal or plates, and further groups take the accent.
